key_insight: A reinforcement-learning policy adaptively chooses the deviation bound in a sequence of mixed-integer reoptimizations to recover feasible log-truck schedules while tracing a strong stability–cost Pareto front.
engineering_relevance: This gives forestry dispatchers faster real-time recovery plans after disruptions, with better trade-offs between staying close to the original schedule and minimizing operational cost.
method: Model recovery as neighborhood-restricted MILPs indexed by deviation bound k.
Compute the minimum feasible deviation k_min exactly to anchor the search.
Use REINFORCE to adaptively pick successive k values from solver feedback and stop when gains diminish.
evidence_signal: On weekly historical instances from a Canadian forestry partner across all disruption types, the method produced richer Pareto fronts with fewer solver calls than fixed-grid and dichotomic baselines and remained within operational reoptimization times.
watch_item: Performance depends on solver feedback quality and training data coverage, so the learned policy may need retraining or retuning when disruption patterns or fleet operations change.
paper_title: Learning to recover: Adaptive local branching with reinforcement learning for log-truck routing and scheduling under disruptions
